positive_triggers: Preserve useful questions from this lesson in my agreed topic bank.
Quiz me from my active topic bank and withhold the answer key until I try.
negative_triggers: Teach me a topic without saving anything to a question bank.
Read every topic bank before this lesson on one active topic.

behavioral_evaluation.prompt: In an isolated fixture, the learner has agreed to use a private central QUESTION-BANK.md index linking to topics/arrays/QUESTION-BANK.md. The only source material needed is topics/arrays/README.md, which states: arrays store elements contiguously and use zero-based indices; direct access computes an element address from the base address and index, so index access is O(1); linear search is O(n); binary search on sorted arrays is O(log n) because it halves the candidate range. User turn 1: “Add two reusable questions from today’s arrays lesson to the agreed bank, then quiz me on the first. Do not record my attempts.” The first question should ask for the complexity and reason for direct array index access. After the agent asks that question, user turn 2: “O(1), because the array can calculate the element offset from its base address.” Evaluate both turns.
pass_criteria: Uses the agreed central index and only the active topic bank and source; does not load unrelated topic banks.
Adds two distinct, accurate, source-grounded questions with learning objectives, type or difficulty, answer keys or rubrics, explanations, and source references.
Marks uncertainty or source gaps for review and does not present generated practice as an official exam question.
Writes only to the agreed topic bank and does not create an attempt log or journal entry.
Asks the first question without showing its answer key or revealing the expected answer.
After the learner responds, gives feedback based on the answer key and source without claiming broad mastery from one answer.
